The current research suggests that assessing joint line positions using radiographs of the contralateral knee can be a valuable new approach for planning knee revision surgery. The most precise parameter found in this assessment method is the distance between the fibular head and the joint line (JL), which corresponds to the tibia-first technique in revision surgery.

This new approach has shown promising results, as indicated by studies showing that the JL measured using radiographs of the contralateral knee provides an accurate assessment of the joint line. Additionally, other parameters such as level of arthritis, age, gender, visibility of landmarks, and misalignment did not significantly influence measurement accuracy in this study.

Furthermore, a recent study demonstrated that the JL is the first tibial-related landmark for assessing the JL in revision surgery, which aligns with the suggested approach in the research. This new assessment method has the potential to provide more accurate and reliable joint line positions during knee revision surgery, potentially leading to improved outcomes and reduced complications.

While further studies are needed to confirm these findings, the current evidence suggests that radiographic assessments of the JL can be a valuable addition to the planning process for knee revision surgery.
